Baptism is a Sacrament, in which a man who believes, having his body thrice plunged in water in the name of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, dies to the carnal life of sin, and is born again of the Holy Ghost to a life spiritual and holy. Except a, man be born of water and, of the Spirit, he can not enter into the kingdom of God. John iii. 5.
documents.locator: Q. 288 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 289 — When and how began Baptism?
documents.text:
289. When and how began Baptism?

First, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus. Acts xix. 4. Afterwards, Jesus Christ, by his own example, sanctified Baptism, when he received it from John. Lastly, after his resurrection, he gave the Apostles this solemn commandment: Go ye and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Matt. xxviii. 19.
documents.locator: Q. 289 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 290 — What is most essential in the administration of Baptism?
documents.text:
290. What is most essential in the administration of Baptism?

Trine immersion in water, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
documents.locator: Q. 290 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 291 — What is required of him that seeks to be baptized?
documents.text:
291. What is required of him that seeks to be baptized?

Repentance and faith; for which cause, also, before Baptism the? recite the Creed. Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost. Acts ii. 38. He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved. Mark xvi. 16.
documents.locator: Q. 291 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 292 — But why, then, are children baptized?
documents.text:
292. But why, then, are children baptized?

For the faith of their parents and sponsors, who are also bound to teach them the faith so soon as they are of sufficient age to learn.
documents.locator: Q. 292 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 293 — How can you show from holy Scripture that we ought to baptize infants?
documents.text:
293. How can you show from holy Scripture that we ought to baptize infants?

In the time of the Old Testament, infants were circumcised when eight days old; but Baptism in the New Testament takes the place of circumcision; consequently infants should also be baptized.
documents.locator: Q. 293 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 294 — Whence does it appear that Baptism takes the place of circumcision?
documents.text:
294. Whence does it appear that Baptism takes the place of circumcision?

From the following words of the Apostle to believers: Ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ, buried with him in Baptism. Coloss. ii. 11, 12.
documents.locator: Q. 294 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 295 — Why are there sponsors at Baptism?
documents.text:
295. Why are there sponsors at Baptism?

In order that they may stand sureties before the Church for the faith of the baptized, and after Baptism may take him in charge, to confirm him in the faith. (See Dion. Areop. on the Eccl. Hier. cap. ii.)
documents.locator: Q. 295 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 296 — Why before baptizing do we use exorcism?
documents.text:
296. Why before baptizing do we use exorcism?

To drive away the devil, who since Adam's fall has had access to men, and power over them, as his captives and slaves.

The Apostle Paul says, that all men, without grace, walk according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience. Eph. ii. 2.
documents.locator: Q. 296 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 297 — Wherein lies the force of exorcism?
documents.text:
297. Wherein lies the force of exorcism?

In the name of Jesus Christ, invoked with prayer and faith. Jesus Christ gave to believers this promise: In my name shall they cast out devils. Mark xvi. 17.
documents.locator: Q. 297 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 298 — What force has the sign of the cross used on this and other occasions?
documents.text:
298. What force has the sign of the cross used on this and other occasions?

What the name of Jesus Christ crucified is when pronounced with faith by motion of the lips, the very same is also the sign of the cross when made with faith by motion of the hand, or represented in any other way.

Cyril of Jerusalem writes: Let us not be ashamed to confess the Crucified; let us boldly make the sign of the Cross on the forehead, and on every thing; on the bread which we eat; on the cups from which we drink; let us make it at our going out, and coming in; when we lie down to sleep, and when we rise; when we journey, and when we rest: it is a great safeguard, given to the poor without price, to the weak without labor. For this is the grace of God; a token for the faithful, and a terror for evil spirits. (Cat. Lect. xiii. 36.)
documents.locator: Q. 298 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 299 — Whence have we the use of the sign of the Cross?
documents.text:
299. Whence have we the use of the sign of the Cross?

From the very times of the Apostles. (See Dion. Areop. on the Eccl. Hier. cap. ii. and v.; also Tertull. de Coron. cap. iii.; de Resurr. cap. viii.)
documents.locator: Q. 299 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 300 — What means the white garment which is put on after Baptism?
documents.text:
300. What means the white garment which is put on after Baptism?

The purity of the soul, and of the Christian life.
documents.locator: Q. 300 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 301 — Why do they hang upon the baptized a Cross?
documents.text:
301. Why do they hang upon the baptized a Cross?

As a visible expression and continual remembrance of Christ's command: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. Matt. xvi. 24.
documents.locator: Q. 301 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 302 — What means the procession of the baptized round the font with a light?
documents.text:
302. What means the procession of the baptized round the font with a light?

Spiritual joy, joined with spiritual illumination.
documents.locator: Q. 302 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 303 — How is this to be understood, that in the Creed we are made to confess one Baptism?
documents.text:
303. How is this to be understood, that in the Creed we are made to confess one Baptism?

In this sense: that Baptism can not be repeated.
documents.locator: Q. 303 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 304 — Why can not Baptism be repeated?
documents.text:
304. Why can not Baptism be repeated?

Baptism is spiritual birth: a man is born but once; therefore he is also baptized but once.
documents.locator: Q. 304 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 305 — What is to be thought of those who sin after Baptism?
documents.text:
305. What is to be thought of those who sin after Baptism?

That they are more guilty in their sins than the unbaptized, since they had from God special help to do well, and have thrown it away.

For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. 2 Peter ii. 20.
documents.locator: Q. 305 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 306 — But is there not any way even for such as have sinned after Baptism to obtain pardon?
documents.text:
306. But is there not any way even for such as have sinned after Baptism to obtain pardon?

There is a way, which is penitence.
documents.locator: Q. 306 (Part I: On Faith, On Baptism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 307 — What is Unction with Chrism ?
documents.text:
307. What is Unction with Chrism ?

Unction with Chrism is a Sacrament, in which the baptized believer, being anointed with holy chrism on certain parts of the body in the name of the Holy Ghost, receives the gifts of the Holy Ghost for growth and strength in spiritual life.
documents.locator: Q. 307 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 308 — Is this Sacrament mentioned in holy Scripture?
documents.text:
308. Is this Sacrament mentioned in holy Scripture?

The inward grace of this Sacrament is spoken of by the Apostle John, as follows: But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things. And the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you; but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie; and even as it hath taught you, abide therein. 1 John ii. 20, 27.

In like manner the Apostle Paul also says: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God; who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts. 2 Cor. i. 21, 22.

Hence are taken the words pronounced at the Unction: The seal of the gift of the Holy Ghost.
documents.locator: Q. 308 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 309 — Is the outward form of Unction with Chrism mentioned in holy Scripture?
documents.text:
309. Is the outward form of Unction with Chrism mentioned in holy Scripture?

It may well be supposed that the words of St. John refer to a visible as well as to an inward unction; but it is more certain that the Apostles, for imparting to the baptized the gifts of the Holy Ghost, used imposition of hands. Acts viii. 14, 16. The successors of the Apostles, however, in place of this, introduced unction with chrism, drawing, it may be, their precedent from the unction used in the Old Testament. Exod. xxx. 25; 1 (3 in the Greek) Kings i. 39. (Dion. Areop. de Eccl. Hier. cap. iv.)
documents.locator: Q. 309 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 310 — What is to be remarked of the holy Chrism?
documents.text:
310. What is to be remarked of the holy Chrism?

This: that its consecration is reserved to the heads of the Hierarchy, as successors of the Apostles, who used the laying on of their own hands to communicate the gifts of the Holy Ghost.
documents.locator: Q. 310 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 311 — What is specially signified by anointing the forehead?
documents.text:
311. What is specially signified by anointing the forehead?

The sanctification of the mind, or thoughts.
documents.locator: Q. 311 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 312 — What by anointing the chest?
documents.text:
312. What by anointing the chest?

The sanctification of the heart, or desires.
documents.locator: Q. 312 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 313 — What by anointing the eyes, ears, and lips?
documents.text:
313. What by anointing the eyes, ears, and lips?

The sanctification of the senses.
documents.locator: Q. 313 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 314 — What by anointing the hands and feet?
documents.text:
314. What by anointing the hands and feet?

The sanctification of the works and whole walk of the Christian.
documents.locator: Q. 314 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Chrism)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 315 — What is the Communion?
documents.text:
315. What is the Communion?

The Communion is a Sacrament, in which the believer, under the forms of bread and wine, partakes of the very Body and Blood of Christ, to everlasting life.
documents.locator: Q. 315 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 316 — How was this Sacrament instituted?
documents.text:
316. How was this Sacrament instituted?

Jesus Christ, immediately before his passion, consecrated it for the first time, exhibiting in it by anticipation a lively image of his sufferings for our salvation; and after having administered it to the Apostles, he gave them at the same time a commandment ever after to perpetuate this Sacrament.
documents.locator: Q. 316 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 317 — What is to be noticed of the Sacrament of the Communion in regard to divine service in the Church?
documents.text:
317. What is to be noticed of the Sacrament of the Communion in regard to divine service in the Church?

This: that it forms the chief and most essential part of divine service.
documents.locator: Q. 317 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 318 — What is the name of that service in which the Sacrament of the Communion is consecrated?
documents.text:
318. What is the name of that service in which the Sacrament of the Communion is consecrated?

The Liturgy.
documents.locator: Q. 318 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 319 — What means the word Liturgy t
documents.text:
319. What means the word Liturgy t

Common service, but the name Liturgy is specially appropriated to that divine service in which the Sacrament of the Communion is consecrated.
documents.locator: Q. 319 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 320 — What is to be noted of the place where the Liturgy is celebrated?
documents.text:
320. What is to be noted of the place where the Liturgy is celebrated?

It must always be consecrated in a temple, the table in which, or at least, if there be no such table, the antimense on which the Sacrament is consecrated, must have been consecrated by a Bishop.
documents.locator: Q. 320 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 321 — Why is the temple called a church T
documents.text:
321. Why is the temple called a church T

Because the faithful, who compose the Church, meet in it for prayer and Sacraments.
documents.locator: Q. 321 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 322 — Why is the table, on which the Sacrament of the Communion is consecrated, called the throne?
documents.text:
322. Why is the table, on which the Sacrament of the Communion is consecrated, called the throne?

Because on it Jesus Christ, as King, is mystically present.
documents.locator: Q. 322 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 323 — What general order of parts may be remarked in the Liturgy?
documents.text:
323. What general order of parts may be remarked in the Liturgy?

This: that first the elements are prepared for the Sacrament; secondly, the faithful are prepared for the Sacrament; lastly, the Sacrament itself is consecrated.
documents.locator: Q. 323 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 324 — What is the name for that part of the Liturgy in which the elements are prepared for the Sacrament?
documents.text:
324. What is the name for that part of the Liturgy in which the elements are prepared for the Sacrament?

Proskomidè, προσκομιδή .
documents.locator: Q. 324 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 325 — What is the meaning of the word Proskomidè?
documents.text:
325. What is the meaning of the word Proskomidè?

Offertory.
documents.locator: Q. 325 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 326 — Why is this name given to the first part of the Liturgy?
documents.text:
326. Why is this name given to the first part of the Liturgy?

From the custom of the primitive Christians to offer in the Church bread and wine for the celebration of the Sacrament. On the same account this bread is called prosphora, which means oblation.
documents.locator: Q. 326 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 327 — In what consists the Offertory, as a part of the Liturgy?
documents.text:
327. In what consists the Offertory, as a part of the Liturgy?

In this: that with mention made of the prophecies and types, and partly also of the events themselves, relating to the birth and suffering of Jesus Christ, a portion is taken from the prosphora for use in the Sacrament, and likewise a portion of wine mixed with water is poured off into the holy chalice, while the celebrator makes commemoration of the whole Church, honors the glorified saints, prays for the living and the departed, especially for the ruling powers, and for those who, of their own faith and zeal, have brought prosphoræ, or oblations.
documents.locator: Q. 327 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 328 — Of what kind should be the bread for the Sacrament?
documents.text:
328. Of what kind should be the bread for the Sacrament?

Such as the name itself of bread, the holiness of the Mystery, and the example of Jesus Christ and the Apostles all require; that is, leavened, pure, wheaten bread.
documents.locator: Q. 328 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 329 — What is signified by this, that the bread or loaf which is strictly to be used for the Communion is only one T
documents.text:
329. What is signified by this, that the bread or loaf which is strictly to be used for the Communion is only one T

It signifies, as the Apostle explains, that we, being many, are one bread, and one body; for we are all partakers of that one bread. lCor.x.17.
documents.locator: Q. 329 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 330 — Why is the bread, when prepared for the Communion, called the Lamb?
documents.text:
330. Why is the bread, when prepared for the Communion, called the Lamb?

Because it is the figure of Jesus Christ suffering, as was in the Old Testament the Paschal Lamb.
documents.locator: Q. 330 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 331 — What was the Paschal Lamb?
documents.text:
331. What was the Paschal Lamb?

The lamb which the Israelites, by God's command, killed and ate in memory of their deliverance from destruction in Egypt.
documents.locator: Q. 331 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 332 — Why is the wine for the Sacrament of the Communion mixed with water?
documents.text:
332. Why is the wine for the Sacrament of the Communion mixed with water?

Because the whole of this celebration is ordered so as to figure forth the sufferings of Christ; and when he suffered there flowed from his pierced side blood and water.
documents.locator: Q. 332 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 333 — What name has that part of the Liturgy in which the faithful are prepared for the Sacrament?
documents.text:
333. What name has that part of the Liturgy in which the faithful are prepared for the Sacrament?

The ancients called it the Liturgy of the Catechumens; because, besides baptized communicants, the catechumens, also, who are preparing for Baptism, and the penitents, who are not admitted to communion, may be present at it.
documents.locator: Q. 333 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 334 — With what does this part of the Liturgy begin?
documents.text:
334. With what does this part of the Liturgy begin?

With the Blessing, or glorification of the Kingdom of the Most Holy Trinity.
documents.locator: Q. 334 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 335 — In what consists this part of the Liturgy?
documents.text:
335. In what consists this part of the Liturgy?

In prayers, singing, and reading from the books of the Apostles, and from the Gospel.
documents.locator: Q. 335 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 336 — "With what does it end?
documents.text:
336. "With what does it end?

With the order given to the catechumens to go out and leave the church.
documents.locator: Q. 336 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 337 — What is the name for that part of the Liturgy in which the Sacrament itself is celebrated and consecrated?
documents.text:
337. What is the name for that part of the Liturgy in which the Sacrament itself is celebrated and consecrated?

The Liturgy of the Faithful; because the faithful only, that is, the baptized, have the right to be present at this service.
documents.locator: Q. 337 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 338 — What is the most essential act in this part of the Liturgy?
documents.text:
338. What is the most essential act in this part of the Liturgy?

The utterance of the words which Jesus Christ spake in instituting the Sacrament: Take, eat; this is my body. Drink ye all of it; for this is my Blood of the New Testament. Matt. xxvi. 26, 27, 28. And after this the invocation of the Holy Ghost, and the blessing the gifts, that is, the bread and wine which have been offered.
documents.locator: Q. 338 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 339 — Why is this so essential?
documents.text:
339. Why is this so essential?

Because at the moment of this act the bread and wine are changed, or transubstantiated, into the very Body of Christ, and into the very Blood of Christ.
documents.locator: Q. 339 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 340 — How are we to understand the word transubstantiation T
documents.text:
340. How are we to understand the word transubstantiation T

In the exposition of the faith by the Eastern Patriarchs, it is said that the word transubstantiation is not to be taken to define the manner in which the bread and wine are changed into the Body and Blood of the Lord; for this none can understand but God; but only thus much is signified, that the bread truly, really, and substantially becomes the very true Body of the Lord, and the wine the very Blood of the Lord. In like manner John Damascene, treating of the Holy and Immaculate Mysteries of the Lord, writes thus: It is truly that Body, united with Godhead, which had its origin from the Holy Virgin; not as though that Body which ascended came down from heaven, but because the bread and wine themselves are changed into the Body and Blood of God. But if thou seekest after the manner how this is, let it suffice thee to be told that it is by the Holy Ghost; in like manner as, by the same Holy Ghost, the Lord formed flesh to himself, and in himself, from the Mother of God; nor know I aught more than this, that the Word of God is true, powerful, and almighty, but its manner of operation unsearchable. (J. Damasc. Theol. lib. iv. cap. 13, § 7.)
documents.locator: Q. 340 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 341 — What is required individually of every one who desires to approach the Sacrament of the Communion?
documents.text:
341. What is required individually of every one who desires to approach the Sacrament of the Communion?

To examine his conscience before God, and to cleanse it from sin by penitence; for doing which he has helps in fasting and prayer.

Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup; for he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh damnation to himself, not discerning the Lord's Body. 1 Cor. xi. 28, 29.
documents.locator: Q. 341 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 342 — What benefit does he receive who communicates in the Body and Blood of Christ?
documents.text:
342. What benefit does he receive who communicates in the Body and Blood of Christ?

He is in the closest manner united to Jesus Christ himself, and, in him, is made partaker of everlasting life.

He that eateth my Flesh, and drinketh my Blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him. John vi. 56. Whoso eateth my Flesh, and drinketh my Blood, hath eternal life. John vi. 54.
documents.locator: Q. 342 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 343 — Ought we to communicate often in the holy Mysteries?
documents.text:
343. Ought we to communicate often in the holy Mysteries?

The primitive Christians communicated every Lord's Day; but now few have such purity of life as to be always prepared to approach so great a Mystery. Our Mother the Church calls on all, who would live religiously, to confess before their ghostly Father, and communicate in the Body and Blood of Christ, four times yearly, or even every month, but requires all, without exception, to receive it at the least once in the year. (See Orthod. Confess. Pt. I. Q. 90.)
documents.locator: Q. 343 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 344 — What part can they have in the divine Liturgy who only hear it without approaching the holy Communion?
documents.text:
344. What part can they have in the divine Liturgy who only hear it without approaching the holy Communion?

They may and should take part in the Liturgy by prayer and faith, and especially by a continual remembrance of our Lord Jesus Christ, who expressly has commanded us to do this in remembrance of him. Luke xxii. 19.
documents.locator: Q. 344 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 345 — What should we remember at that time in the Liturgy when they make the Procession with the Gospel?
documents.text:
345. What should we remember at that time in the Liturgy when they make the Procession with the Gospel?

Jesus Christ appearing to preach the Gospel. So also while the Gospel is reading, we should have the same attention and reverence as if we saw and heard Jesus Christ himself.
documents.locator: Q. 345 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 346 — What should we remember at that time in the Liturgy when they make the Procession with the gifts from the table of preparation to the altar?
documents.text:
346. What should we remember at that time in the Liturgy when they make the Procession with the gifts from the table of preparation to the altar?

Jesus Christ going to suffer voluntarily, as a victim to the slaughter, while more than twelve legions of angels were ready around to guard him as their King.

The King of kings, and Lord of lords, cometh to be slaughtered. (Hymn for the Liturgy on the Great Sabbath.)
documents.locator: Q. 346 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 347 — What should we remember at the moment of the consecration of the Sacrament, and while the clergy are communicating within the altar?
documents.text:
347. What should we remember at the moment of the consecration of the Sacrament, and while the clergy are communicating within the altar?

The mystical supper of Jesus Christ himself with his Apostles; his suffering, death, and burial.
documents.locator: Q. 347 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 348 — What is set forth after this, by the drawing back of the veil, the opening of the royal doors, and the appearance of the holy gifts?
documents.text:
348. What is set forth after this, by the drawing back of the veil, the opening of the royal doors, and the appearance of the holy gifts?

The appearance of Jesus Christ himself after his resurrection.
documents.locator: Q. 348 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 349 — What is figured by the last showing of the holy gifts to the people, after which they are hid from view?
documents.text:
349. What is figured by the last showing of the holy gifts to the people, after which they are hid from view?

The ascension of Jesus Christ into heaven.
documents.locator: Q. 349 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 350 — Will the use of the Sacrament of the holy Communion continue ever in the true Church of Christ?
documents.text:
350. Will the use of the Sacrament of the holy Communion continue ever in the true Church of Christ?

Assuredly it will ever continue, even to Christ's coming again, agreeably to the words of the Apostle Paul: For as oft as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do show forth the Lord's death till he come. 1 Cor. xi. 26.
documents.locator: Q. 350 (Part I: On Faith, On the Communion)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 351 — What is Penitence?
documents.text:
351. What is Penitence?

Penitence is a Sacrament, in which he who confesses his sins is, on the outward declaration of pardon by the priest, inwardly loosed from his sins by Jesus Christ himself.
documents.locator: Q. 351 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 352 — What is the origin of this Sacrament?
documents.text:
352. What is the origin of this Sacrament?

They who came to John the Baptist, who preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins, confessed their sins. Mark i. 4, 5. The Apostles were promised by Jesus Christ power to forgive sins, when he said, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven. Matt. xviii. 18. And after his resurrection he actually gave them this power, saying, Receive ye the Holy Ghost: whosesoever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them and whosesoever sins ye retain, they are retained. John xx. 22, 23.
documents.locator: Q. 352 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 353 — What is required of the penitent?
documents.text:
353. What is required of the penitent?

Contrition for his sins, with a full purpose of amendment of life, faith in Jesus Christ, and hope in his mercy.

For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation, not to be repented of. 2 Cor. vii. 10. But if the wicked turn from his wickedness, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby. Ezek. xxxiii. 19. To him, that is to Jesus Christ, give all the Prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins. Acts x. 43.
documents.locator: Q. 353 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 354 — Are there not besides certain preparations and aids to Penitence?
documents.text:
354. Are there not besides certain preparations and aids to Penitence?

Such are fasting and prayer.
documents.locator: Q. 354 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 355 — Is there not besides these a certain special mean used by holy Church for cleansing and giving peace to the conscience of the penitent?
documents.text:
355. Is there not besides these a certain special mean used by holy Church for cleansing and giving peace to the conscience of the penitent?

Such a mean is the epitimia, or penance.
documents.locator: Q. 355 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 356 — What is the epitimia?
documents.text:
356. What is the epitimia?

The word means punishment. See 2 Cor. ii. 6. Under this name are prescribed to the penitent, according as may be requisite, divers particular exercises of piety, and divers abstinences or privations, serving to efface the unrighteousness of sin, and to subdue sinful habit; as, for instance, fasting beyond what is prescribed for all, or for grievous sins suspension from the holy Communion for a given time.
documents.locator: Q. 356 (Part I: On Faith, On Penitence)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 357 — What are Orders t
documents.text:
357. What are Orders t

Orders are a Sacrament, in which the Holy Ghost, by the laying on of the Bishop's hands, ordains them that be rightly chosen to minister sacraments, and to feed the flock of Christ.

Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. 1 Cor. iv. 1.

Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the Church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood. Acts xx. 28.
documents.locator: Q. 357 (Part I: On Faith, On Orders)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 358 — What is it to feed the Church?
documents.text:
358. What is it to feed the Church?

To instruct the people in faith, piety, and good works.
documents.locator: Q. 358 (Part I: On Faith, On Orders)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 359 — How many necessary degrees are there of Orders?
documents.text:
359. How many necessary degrees are there of Orders?

Three: those of Bishop, Priest, and Deacon.
documents.locator: Q. 359 (Part I: On Faith, On Orders)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 360 — What difference is there between them?
documents.text:
360. What difference is there between them?

The Deacon serves at the Sacraments; the Priest hallows Sacraments in dependence on the Bishop; the Bishop not only hallows the Sacraments himself, but has power also to impart to others, by the laying on of his hands, the gift and grace to hallow them.

Of the Episcopal power the Apostle Paul thus writes to Titus: For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city. Titus i. 5. And to Timothy: Lay hands suddenly on no man. 1 Tim. v. 22.
documents.locator: Q. 360 (Part I: On Faith, On Orders)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 361 — What is Matrimony?
documents.text:
361. What is Matrimony?

Matrimony is a Sacrament, in which, on the free promise of the man and woman before the priest and the Church to be true to each other, their conjugal union is blessed to be an image of Christ's union with the Church, and grace is asked for them to live together in godly love and honesty, to the procreation and Christian bringing up of children.
documents.locator: Q. 361 (Part I: On Faith, On Matrimony)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 362 — Whence does it appear that Matrimony is a Sacrament?
documents.text:
362. Whence does it appear that Matrimony is a Sacrament?

From the following words of the Apostle Paul: A man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. This Sacrament is great: but I speak concerning Christ and the Church. Eph. v. 31, 32.
documents.locator: Q. 362 (Part I: On Faith, On Matrimony)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 363 — Is it the duty of all to marry?
documents.text:
363. Is it the duty of all to marry?

No. Virginity is better than wedlock, if any have the gift to keep it undefiled.

Of this Jesus Christ has said expressly: All men can not receive this saying, save they to whom it is given. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it. Matt. xix. 11, 12.

And the Apostle says: I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I; but if they can not contain, let them marry. . . . He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord; but he that is I married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife. . . . He that giveth his virgin in marriage doeth well; but he that giveth her not in marriage doeth better. 1 Cor. vii. 8, 9, 32, 33, 38.
documents.locator: Q. 363 (Part I: On Faith, On Matrimony)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 364 — What is Unction with Oil? I
documents.text:
364. What is Unction with Oil? I

Unction with Oil is a Sacrament, in which, while the body is anointed with oil, God's grace is invoked on the sick, to heal him of spiritual and bodily infirmities.
documents.locator: Q. 364 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Oil)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 365 — Whence is the origin of this Sacrament?
documents.text:
365. Whence is the origin of this Sacrament?

From the Apostles, who, having received power from Jesus Christ, anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them. Mark vi. 13.

The Apostles left this Sacrament to the priests of the Church, as is evident from the following words of the Apostle James: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the Church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. James v. 14, 16.
documents.locator: Q. 365 (Part I: On Faith, On Unction with Oil)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 366 — What is the resurrection of the dead, which, in the words of the Creed, we look for or expect?
documents.text:
366. What is the resurrection of the dead, which, in the words of the Creed, we look for or expect?

An act of the almighty power of God, by which all bodies of dead men, being reunited to their souls, shall return to life, and shall thenceforth be spiritual and immortal.

It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body. 1 Cor. xv. 44. For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality. 1 Cor. xv. 53.
documents.locator: Q. 366 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 367 — How shall the body rise again after it has rotted and perished in the ground?
documents.text:
367. How shall the body rise again after it has rotted and perished in the ground?

Since God formed the body from the ground originally, he can equally restore it after it has perished in the ground. The Apostle Paul illustrates this by the analogy of a grain of seed, which rots in the earth, but from which there springs up afterwards a plant, or tree. That which thou sowest is not quickened except it die. 1 Cor. xv. 36.
documents.locator: Q. 367 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 368 — Shall all, strictly speaking, rise again?
documents.text:
368. Shall all, strictly speaking, rise again?

All, without exception, that have died; but they who at the time of the general resurrection shall be still alive shall have their present gross bodies changed in a moment, so as to become spiritual and immortal.

We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump; for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed. 1 Cor. xv. 51, 52.
documents.locator: Q. 368 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 369 — When shall the resurrection of the dead be?
documents.text:
369. When shall the resurrection of the dead be?

At the end of this visible world?
documents.locator: Q. 369 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 370 — Shall the world then too come to an end?
documents.text:
370. Shall the world then too come to an end?

Yes; this corruptible world shall come to an end, and shall be transformed into another, incorruptible.

Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. Rom. viii. 21. Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness. 2 Peter iii. 13.
documents.locator: Q. 370 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 371 — How shall the world be transformed?
documents.text:
371. How shall the world be transformed?

By fire. The heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same, that is, by God's word, are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. 2 Peter iii. 7.
documents.locator: Q. 371 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 372 — In what state are the souls of the dead till the general resurrection?
documents.text:
372. In what state are the souls of the dead till the general resurrection?

The souls of the righteous are in light and rest, with a foretaste of eternal happiness; but the souls of the wicked are in a state the reverse of this.
documents.locator: Q. 372 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 373 — Why may we not ascribe to the souls of the righteous perfect happiness immediately after death?
documents.text:
373. Why may we not ascribe to the souls of the righteous perfect happiness immediately after death?

Because it is ordained that the perfect retribution according to works shall be received by the perfect man after the resurrection of the body and God's last judgment.

The Apostle Paul says: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, shall give me at that day; and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. 2 Tim. iv. 8. And again: We must all appear before the judgment-seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad. 2 Cor. v. 10.
documents.locator: Q. 373 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 374 — Why do we ascribe to the souls of the righteous a foretaste of bliss before the last judgment?
documents.text:
374. Why do we ascribe to the souls of the righteous a foretaste of bliss before the last judgment?

On the testimony of Jesus Christ himself, who says in the parable that the righteous Lazarus was immediately after death carried into Abraham's bosom. Luke xvi. 22.
documents.locator: Q. 374 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 375 — Is this foretaste of bliss joined with a sight of Christ's own countenance?
documents.text:
375. Is this foretaste of bliss joined with a sight of Christ's own countenance?

It is so more especially with the saints, as we are given to understand by the Apostle Paul, who had a desire to depart, and to be with Christ. Phil. i. 23.
documents.locator: Q. 375 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 376 — What is to be remarked of such souls as have departed with faith, but without having had time to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance?
documents.text:
376. What is to be remarked of such souls as have departed with faith, but without having had time to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance?

This: that they may be aided towards the attainment of a blessed resurrection by prayers offered in their behalf, especially such as are offered in union with the oblation of the bloodless sacrifice of the Body and Blood of Christ, and by works of mercy done in faith for their memory.
documents.locator: Q. 376 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 377 — On what is this doctrine grounded?
documents.text:
377. On what is this doctrine grounded?

On the constant tradition of the Catholic Church; the sources of which may be seen even in the Church of the Old Testament. Judas Maccabæus offered sacrifice for his men that had fallen. 2 Macc. xii. 43. Prayer for the departed has ever formed a fixed part of the divine Liturgy, from the first Liturgy of the Apostle James. St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: Very great will be the benefit to those souls for which prayer is offered at the moment when the holy and tremendous Sacrifice is lying in view. (Lect. Myst. v. 9.)

St. Basil the Great, in his prayers for Pentecost, says that the Lord vouchsafes to receive from us propitiatory prayers and sacrifices for those that are kept in Hades, and allows us the hope of obtaining for them peace, relief, and freedom.
documents.locator: Q. 377 (Part I: On Faith, On the Eleventh Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 378 — What is the life of the world to come T
documents.text:
378. What is the life of the world to come T

The life that shall be after the resurrection of the dead and the general judgment of Christ.
documents.locator: Q. 378 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 379 — What kind of life shall this be?
documents.text:
379. What kind of life shall this be?

For those who believe, who love God, and do what is good, it shall be so happy that we can not now even conceive such happiness. It doth not yet appear what we shall be. 1 John iii. 2. I knew a man in Christ, says the Apostle Paul, who was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. 2 Cor. xii. 2, 4.
documents.locator: Q. 379 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 380 — Whence shall proceed this so great happiness?
documents.text:
380. Whence shall proceed this so great happiness?

From the contemplation of God in light and glory, and from union with him. For now we see through a glass darkly, but then face to face: now I know in part, but then shall I know, even as also I am known. 1 Cor. xiii. 12.

Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father. Matt. xiii. 43. God shall be all in all. 1 Cor. xv. 28.
documents.locator: Q. 380 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 381 — Shall the body also share in the happiness of the soul?
documents.text:
381. Shall the body also share in the happiness of the soul?

Yes; it too will be glorified with the light of God, as Christ's body was at his transfiguration on Mount Tabor.

It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. 1 Cor. xv. 43. As we have borne the image of the earthy, that is, of Adam, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly. 1 Cor. xv. 49.
documents.locator: Q. 381 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 382 — Will all be equally happy?
documents.text:
382. Will all be equally happy?

No. There will be different degrees of happiness, in proportion as every one shall have here endured the fight of faith, love, and good works. There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differeth from another star in glory. So also is the resurrection of the dead. 1 Cor. xv. 41, 42.
documents.locator: Q. 382 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 383 — But what will be the lot of unbelievers and transgressors?
documents.text:
383. But what will be the lot of unbelievers and transgressors?

They will be given over to everlasting death—that is, to everlasting fire, to everlasting torment, with the devils.

Whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire. Rev. xx. 15. And, That is the second death. Rev. xx. 14. Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels. Matt. xxv. 41. And these shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life eternal. Matt. xxv 46. It is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. Mark ix. 47, 48.
documents.locator: Q. 383 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 384 — Why will such severity be used with sinners?
documents.text:
384. Why will such severity be used with sinners?

Not because God willed them to perish; but they of their own will perish, because they receive not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. 2 Thess. ii. 10.
documents.locator: Q. 384 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 385 — Of what benefit will it be to us to meditate on death, on the resurrection, on the last judgment, on everlasting happiness, and on everlasting torment?
documents.text:
385. Of what benefit will it be to us to meditate on death, on the resurrection, on the last judgment, on everlasting happiness, and on everlasting torment?

These meditations will assist us to abstain from sin, and to wean our affections from earthly things; they will console ns for the absence or loss of worldly goods, incite us to keep our souls and bodies pure, to live to God and to eternity, and so to attain everlasting salvation.
documents.locator: Q. 385 (Part I: On Faith, On the Twelfth Article)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 386 — What is Christian hope?
documents.text:
386. What is Christian hope?

The resting of the heart on God, with the full trust that he ever cares for our salvation, and will give us the happiness he has promised.
documents.locator: Q. 386 (Part II: On Hope, Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto)
keywords: Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 387 — What is the ground of Christian hope?
documents.text:
387. What is the ground of Christian hope?

The Lord Jesus Christ is our hope, or the ground of our hope. 1 Tim. i. 1. Hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you by the revelation of Jesus Christ. 1 Peter i. 13.
documents.locator: Q. 387 (Part II: On Hope, Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto)
keywords: Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 388 — What are the means for attaining to a saving hope?
documents.text:
388. What are the means for attaining to a saving hope?

The means to this are, first, prayer; secondly, the true doctrine of blessedness, and its practical application.
documents.locator: Q. 388 (Part II: On Hope, Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto)
keywords: Definition of Christian Hope, its Ground, and the Means thereto

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 389 — Is there any testimony of God's Word to this, that prayer is a mean for attaining to a saving hope?
documents.text:
389. Is there any testimony of God's Word to this, that prayer is a mean for attaining to a saving hope?

Jesus Christ himself joins the hope of receiving our desire with prayer: Whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. John xiv. 13.
documents.locator: Q. 389 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 390 — What is Prayer?
documents.text:
390. What is Prayer?

The lifting up of man's mind and heart to God, manifested by devout words.
documents.locator: Q. 390 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 391 — What should the Christian do when he lifts up his mind and heart to God?
documents.text:
391. What should the Christian do when he lifts up his mind and heart to God?

First, he should glorify him for his divine perfections; secondly, give thanks to him for his mercies; thirdly, ask him for what he needs. So there are three chief forms of prayer: Praise, Thanksgiving, and Petition.
documents.locator: Q. 391 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 392 — Can a man pray without words?
documents.text:
392. Can a man pray without words?

He can: in mind and heart. An example of this may be seen in Moses before the passage through the Red Sea. Exod. xiv. 15.
documents.locator: Q. 392 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 393 — Has not such prayer a name of its own?
documents.text:
393. Has not such prayer a name of its own?

It is called spiritual, or prayer of the heart and mind, in one word, inward prayer; while, on the other hand, prayer expressed in words, and accompanied by other marks of devotion, is called oral or outward prayer.
documents.locator: Q. 393 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 394 — Can there be outward prayer without inward?
documents.text:
394. Can there be outward prayer without inward?

There can: if any man utter words of prayer without attention or earnestness.
documents.locator: Q. 394 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 395 — Does outward prayer alone suffice to obtain grace?
documents.text:
395. Does outward prayer alone suffice to obtain grace?

So far is it from sufficing to obtain grace, that contrariwise it provokes God to anger.

God has himself declared his displeasure at such prayer: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoreth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me: but in vain do they worship me. Matt. xv. 8, 9.
documents.locator: Q. 395 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 396 — Does not inward prayer alone suffice without outward?
documents.text:
396. Does not inward prayer alone suffice without outward?

This question is as if one should ask whether soul alone might not suffice for man without body. It is idle to ask this, seeing that God has been pleased to make man consist of soul and body; likewise idle it is to ask whether inward prayer alone may not suffice without outward. Since we have both soul and body, we ought to glorify God in our bodies, and in our souls, which are God's: this being besides natural, that out of the abundance of the heart the mouth should speak. Our Lord Jesus Christ was spiritual in the highest degree, but even he expressed his spiritual prayer both by words and by devout gestures of body, sometimes, for instance, lifting up his eyes to heaven, sometimes kneeling, or falling on his face to the ground. 1 Cor. vi. 20; Matt. xii. 34; John xvii. 1; Luke xxii. 41; Matt. xxvi. 39.
documents.locator: Q. 396 (Part II: On Hope, On Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 397 — Is there not a prayer which may be termed the common Christian prayer, and pattern of all prayers?
documents.text:
397. Is there not a prayer which may be termed the common Christian prayer, and pattern of all prayers?

Such is the Lord's Prayer.
documents.locator: Q. 397 (Part II: On Hope, On the Lord's Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 398 — What is the Lord's Prayer?
documents.text:
398. What is the Lord's Prayer?

A prayer which our Lord Jesus Christ taught the Apostles, and which they delivered to all believers.
documents.locator: Q. 398 (Part II: On Hope, On the Lord's Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 399 — Repeat it.
documents.locator: Q. 399 (Part II: On Hope, On the Lord's Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 400 — In order the better to understand the Lord's Prayer, how may we divide it?
documents.text:
400. In order the better to understand the Lord's Prayer, how may we divide it?

Into the invocation, seven petitions, and the doxology.
documents.locator: Q. 400 (Part II: On Hope, On the Lord's Prayer)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 401 — How dare we call God Father?
documents.text:
401. How dare we call God Father?

By faith in Jesus Christ, and by the grace of regeneration.

As many as received him, to them, gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name: which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. John i. 12, 13.
documents.locator: Q. 401 (Part II: On Hope, On the Invocation)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 402 — Must we say Our Father even when we pray alone?
documents.text:
402. Must we say Our Father even when we pray alone?

Certainly we must.
documents.locator: Q. 402 (Part II: On Hope, On the Invocation)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 403 — Why so?
documents.text:
403. Why so?

Because Christian charity requires us to call upon God, and ask good things of him, for all our brethren, no less than for ourselves.
documents.locator: Q. 403 (Part II: On Hope, On the Invocation)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 404 — Why in the invocation do we say, Who art in heaven?
documents.text:
404. Why in the invocation do we say, Who art in heaven?

That, entering upon prayer, we may leave every thing earthly and corruptible, and raise our minds and hearts to what is heavenly, everlasting, and divine.
documents.locator: Q. 404 (Part II: On Hope, On the Invocation)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 405 — Is not God's name holy?
documents.text:
405. Is not God's name holy?

Doubtless it is holy in itself. Holy is his name. Luke i. 49.
documents.locator: Q. 405 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 406 — How, then, can it yet be hallowed?
documents.text:
406. How, then, can it yet be hallowed?

It may be hallowed in men; that is, his eternal holiness may be manifested in them.
documents.locator: Q. 406 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 407 — How?
documents.text:
407. How?

First, when we, having in our thoughts and heart the name of God, so live as his holiness requires, and thus glorify God; secondly, when others also, seeing our good lives, glorify God.

Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Matt. v. 16.
documents.locator: Q. 407 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 408 — What is the kingdom of God spoken of in the second petition of the Lord's Prayer?
documents.text:
408. What is the kingdom of God spoken of in the second petition of the Lord's Prayer?

The kingdom of grace, which, as St. Paul says, is righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost. Rom. xiv. 17.
documents.locator: Q. 408 (Part II: On Hope, On the Second Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 409 — Is not this kingdom come already?
documents.text:
409. Is not this kingdom come already?

To some it has not yet come in its full sense; while to others it has not yet come at all inasmuch as sin still reigns in their mortal bodies, that they should obey it in the lusts thereof. Rom. vi. 12.
documents.locator: Q. 409 (Part II: On Hope, On the Second Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 410 — How does it come?
documents.text:
410. How does it come?

Secretly, and inwardly. The kingdom of God cometh not with observation; for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you. Luke xvii. 20, 21.
documents.locator: Q. 410 (Part II: On Hope, On the Second Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 411 — May not the Christian ask for something further under the name of God's kingdom?
documents.text:
411. May not the Christian ask for something further under the name of God's kingdom?

He may ask for the kingdom of glory—that is, for the perfect bliss of the faithful.

Having a desire to depart, and be with Christ. Phil. i. 23.
documents.locator: Q. 411 (Part II: On Hope, On the Second Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 412 — What means the petition, Thy will be done?
documents.text:
412. What means the petition, Thy will be done?

Hereby we ask of God that all we do, and all that befalls us, may be ordered not as we will, but as pleases him.
documents.locator: Q. 412 (Part II: On Hope, On the Third Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 413 — Why need we ask this?
documents.text:
413. Why need we ask this?

Because we often err in our wishes; but God unerringly, and incomparably more than we ourselves, wishes for us all that is good, and is ever ready to bestow it, unless he be prevented by our willfulness and obstinacy.

Unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, unto him be glory in the Church. Eph. iii. 20, 21.
documents.locator: Q. 413 (Part II: On Hope, On the Third Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 414 — Why do we ask that God's will be done in earth as in heaven?
documents.text:
414. Why do we ask that God's will be done in earth as in heaven?

Because in heaven the holy angels and saints in bliss, all without exception, always, and in all things, do God's will.
documents.locator: Q. 414 (Part II: On Hope, On the Third Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 415 — What is bread for subsistence?
documents.text:
415. What is bread for subsistence?

The bread which we need in order to subsist or live.
documents.locator: Q. 415 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fourth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 416 — With what thoughts should we ask of God this bread?
documents.text:
416. With what thoughts should we ask of God this bread?

Agreeably with the instruction of our Lord Jesus Christ, we should ask no more than bread for subsistence; that is, necessary food, and such clothing and shelter as is likewise necessary for life; but whatever is beyond this, and serves not so much for necessity as for gratification, we should leave to the will of God; and if it be given, return thanks to him; if it be not given, we should be content without it.
documents.locator: Q. 416 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fourth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 417 — Why are we directed to ask for bread for subsistence only for this day ?
documents.text:
417. Why are we directed to ask for bread for subsistence only for this day ?

That we may not be too anxious about the future, but trust for that to God. Take therefore no thought for the morrow, for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself: sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof. Matt. vi. 34. For your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things. Matt. vi. 32.
documents.locator: Q. 417 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fourth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 418 — May we not ask for something farther under the name of bread for subsistence?
documents.text:
418. May we not ask for something farther under the name of bread for subsistence?

Since man is made of both a bodily and a spiritual substance, and the substance of the soul far excels that of the body, we may and should seek for the soul also that bread of subsistence without which the inward man must perish of hunger.

(See Cyril. Hier. Lect, Myst. iv. 15; Orthod. Confess. Pt. II. Q. 19.)
documents.locator: Q. 418 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fourth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 419 — What is the bread of subsistence for the soul?
documents.text:
419. What is the bread of subsistence for the soul?

The Word of God, and the Body and Blood of Christ.

Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. Matt. iv. 4. My flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. John vi. 55.
documents.locator: Q. 419 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fourth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 420 — What is meant in the Lord's Prayer by our debts?
documents.text:
420. What is meant in the Lord's Prayer by our debts?

Our sins.
documents.locator: Q. 420 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 421 — Why are our sins called debts?
documents.text:
421. Why are our sins called debts?

Because we, having received all from God, ought to render all back to him—that is, subject all to his will and law; which if we do not, we are left debtors to his justice.
documents.locator: Q. 421 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 422 — But who are our debtors?
documents.text:
422. But who are our debtors?

People who have not rendered us that which they owed us by the law of God; as, for instance, have not shown us love, but malice.
documents.locator: Q. 422 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 423 — If God is just, how can we be forgiven our debts?
documents.text:
423. If God is just, how can we be forgiven our debts?

Through the mediation of Jesus Christ.

For there is one God, and one Mediator between God and man, the man Jesus Christ, who gave himself a ransom for all. 1 Tim. ii. 5, 6.
documents.locator: Q. 423 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 424 — What will be the consequence, if we ask God to forgive us our sins without ourselves forgiving others?
documents.text:
424. What will be the consequence, if we ask God to forgive us our sins without ourselves forgiving others?

In that case neither shall we be forgiven.

For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive you your trespasses. Matt. vi. 14, 15.
documents.locator: Q. 424 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 425 — Why will not God forgive us if we do not forgive others?
documents.text:
425. Why will not God forgive us if we do not forgive others?

Because we hereby show ourselves evil, and so alienate from us God's goodness and
documents.locator: Q. 425 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 426 — What disposition, then, must we have to use aright those words of the Lord's Prayer, As we forgive our debtors?
documents.text:
426. What disposition, then, must we have to use aright those words of the Lord's Prayer, As we forgive our debtors?

These words absolutely require that when we pray we should bear no malice nor hatred, but be in peace and charity with all men.

Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and, there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee, leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way: first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift. Matt. v. 23, 24.
documents.locator: Q. 426 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 427 — But what am I to do if I can not readily find him who hath aught against me, or if he show himself unwilling to be reconciled?
documents.text:
427. But what am I to do if I can not readily find him who hath aught against me, or if he show himself unwilling to be reconciled?

In such a case it is enough to be reconciled with him in heart, before the eyes of the all-seeing God.

If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. Rom. xii. 18.
documents.locator: Q. 427 (Part II: On Hope, On the Fifth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 428 — What is meant in the Lord's Prayer by temptation ?
documents.text:
428. What is meant in the Lord's Prayer by temptation ?

Any conjuncture of circumstances in which there is imminent danger of losing the faith, or falling into great sin.
documents.locator: Q. 428 (Part II: On Hope, On the Sixth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 429 — Whence come such temptations?
documents.text:
429. Whence come such temptations?

From our flesh, from the world, or other people, and from the devil.
documents.locator: Q. 429 (Part II: On Hope, On the Sixth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 430 — What do we ask in these words of the prayer, Lead us not into temptation?
documents.text:
430. What do we ask in these words of the prayer, Lead us not into temptation?

First, that God suffer us not to be led into temptation; secondly, that if it be needful for us to be tried and purified through temptation, he give us not up wholly to temptation, nor suffer us to fall.
documents.locator: Q. 430 (Part II: On Hope, On the Sixth Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 431 — What do we ask in these words of the prayer, Deliver as from evil?
documents.text:
431. What do we ask in these words of the prayer, Deliver as from evil?

We ask for deliverance from all evil that can reach us in the world, which since the fall lieth in wickedness (1 John v. 19): but especially from the evil of sin, and from the evil suggestions and snares of the spirit of evil, which is the devil.
documents.locator: Q. 431 (Part II: On Hope, On the Seventh Petition)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 432 — Why after the Lord's Prayer do we subjoin the Doxology?
documents.text:
432. Why after the Lord's Prayer do we subjoin the Doxology?

First, that when we ask mercies for ourselves from our heavenly Father, we may at the same time render him that honor which is his due; secondly, that by the thought of his everlasting kingdom, power, and glory, we may be more and more established in the hope that he will give us what we ask, because this is in his power, and makes to his glory.
documents.locator: Q. 432 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doxology)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 433 — What means the word Amen T
documents.text:
433. What means the word Amen T

It means verily, or so be it.
documents.locator: Q. 433 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doxology)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 434 — Why is this word added to the Doxology?
documents.text:
434. Why is this word added to the Doxology?

To signify that we offer the prayer in faith, and without doubting, as we are taught to do by the Apostle James. James i. 6.
documents.locator: Q. 434 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doxology)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 435 — What must we join with prayer in order to be grounded in the hope of salvation and blessedness?
documents.text:
435. What must we join with prayer in order to be grounded in the hope of salvation and blessedness?

Our own exertions for the attainment of blessedness.

Of this point the Lord himself says: Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? Luke vi. 46. Not every one that saith unto me Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Matt. vii. 21.
documents.locator: Q. 435 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doctrine of Blessedness)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 436 — What doctrine may we take as our guide in these exertions?
documents.text:
436. What doctrine may we take as our guide in these exertions?

The doctrine of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is briefly set forth in his Beatitudes, or sentences on blessedness.
documents.locator: Q. 436 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doctrine of Blessedness)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 437 — How many such sentences are there? The nine following:
documents.text:
437. How many such sentences are there? The nine following:

1. Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

2. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

3. Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

4. Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filed.

5. Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

6. Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

7. Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

8. Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

9. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven. Matt. v. 3-12.
documents.locator: Q. 437 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doctrine of Blessedness)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 438 — What is to be observed of all these sentences in order to their right understanding?
documents.text:
438. What is to be observed of all these sentences in order to their right understanding?

This: that the Lord proposed in these sentences a doctrine for the attainment of blessedness, as is expressly said in the Gospel: He opened his mouth, and taught; but, being meek and lowly of heart, he proposed his doctrine not in the form of commandment, but of blessing, to those who should of their own free will receive and fulfill it. Consequently in each sentence or Beatitude we must consider, first, the doctrine or precept; secondly, the blessing or promise of reward.
documents.locator: Q. 438 (Part II: On Hope, On the Doctrine of Blessedness)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 439 — What is the Lord's first precept of blessedness?
documents.text:
439. What is the Lord's first precept of blessedness?

They who would be blessed must be poor in spirit.
documents.locator: Q. 439 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 440 — What is it to be poor in spirit?
documents.text:
440. What is it to be poor in spirit?

It is to have a spiritual conviction that we have nothing of our own, nothing but what God bestows upon us, and that we can do nothing good without God's help and grace, thus counting ourselves as nothing, and in all throwing ourselves upon the mercy of God; in brief, as St. Chrysostom explains it, spiritual poverty is humility. (Hom. in Matt. xv.)
documents.locator: Q. 440 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 441 — Can the rich, too, be poor in spirit?
documents.text:
441. Can the rich, too, be poor in spirit?

Doubtless they can: if they consider that visible riches are corruptible and soon pass away, and can never compensate for the want of spiritual goods. What is a man profited, if he gain the whole world, and lose his own soul for what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? Matt. xvi. 26.
documents.locator: Q. 441 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 442 — May not bodily poverty serve to the perfection of spiritual?
documents.text:
442. May not bodily poverty serve to the perfection of spiritual?

It may, if the Christian choose it voluntarily, for God's sake. Of this, Jesus Christ himself said to the rich man: If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come and follow me. Matt. xix. 21.
documents.locator: Q. 442 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 443 — What does our Lord promise to the poor in spirit?
documents.text:
443. What does our Lord promise to the poor in spirit?

The kingdom of heaven.
documents.locator: Q. 443 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)

documents.title: Longer Catechism of the Orthodox Church (Philaret) Q. 444 — How is the kingdom of heaven theirs?
documents.text:
444. How is the kingdom of heaven theirs?

In the present life inwardly, and inchoately, by faith and hope; but in the life to come perfectly, by their being made partakers of everlasting blessedness.
documents.locator: Q. 444 (Part II: On Hope, On the First Beatitude)
